# Device setup (`device-setup`)

Pairing a screen with a home server: server address, access token entry or a QR code to scan, and a test step.

Group: Home controls. Styles: `import '@mosaic-home/design-system/css/home';` (or `style.css`).

## Web API

`createDeviceSetup` (types in `dist/web/home/security/deviceSetup.d.ts`): `form.mh-device-setup`: pairs a screen with a home server in three numbered `__step`s: the server address (a URL field), access (a `__method` switch between a pasted access token in the secret field and a QR code: `__qr` shown for a phone to scan, and a `__scan` button that asks the app's scanner and fills in what it read) and a test (`__test` button, then the `__result`: `.is-testing`, `.is-success` or `.is-error`, a polite status). `__actions` holds Cancel and Finish: Finish (or Enter in a field) runs the test first when it hasn't passed yet, and finishes once it does (unless `requireTest` is off). The component sends nothing itself: `onTest`, `onScan` and `onFinish` do the work. The token stays in the password input and the callbacks; it is never logged or written to an attribute.

```ts
export function createDeviceSetup(options: DeviceSetupOptions): DeviceSetupHandle;

export interface DeviceSetupOptions {
  /** Starting address. */
  address?: string;
  /** Starting token (for example from a flash-time file). Never shown unless the user reveals it. */
  token?: string;
  /** The address field's example. */
  placeholder?: string;
  /** The methods offered (default: token, plus QR when `qrValue` or `onScan` is given). */
  methods?: readonly DeviceSetupMethod[];
  method?: DeviceSetupMethod;
  /** A code for a phone to scan (a pairing link from the app); shown in QR mode. */
  qrValue?: string | null;
  /** A line under the title. */
  intro?: string;
  /** Finish runs the test first when it hasn't passed yet (default true). */
  requireTest?: boolean;
  /** Level of the title heading (default 2); steps take the next level. */
  headingLevel?: 2 | 3 | 4 | 5;
  labels?: Partial<DeviceSetupLabels>;
  /** Tests the connection; the component sends nothing itself. */
  onTest?: (values: DeviceSetupValues) => Promise<DeviceSetupResult>;
  /** Opens the app's scanner; resolves to what the code held (or null when cancelled). */
  onScan?: () => Promise<DeviceSetupFill | null>;
  onFinish?: (values: DeviceSetupValues) => void;
  onCancel?: () => void;
  /** Any change of method or values (the token included; keep it out of logs). */
  onChange?: (values: { address: string; token: string; method: DeviceSetupMethod }) => void;
}

export interface DeviceSetupHandle {
  el: HTMLFormElement;
  /** The current values (address normalised, or as typed when it isn't valid). */
  getValues(): DeviceSetupValues;
  /** Fills in values (a delivered pairing, a scan) and resets the test. */
  fill(values: DeviceSetupFill): void;
  /** Runs the test as the button does; resolves to whether it passed. */
  test(): Promise<boolean>;
  update(changes: Partial<Pick<DeviceSetupOptions, 'qrValue' | 'intro' | 'labels' | 'placeholder'>>): void;
}

export interface DeviceSetupLabels {
  title: string;
  addressStep: string;
  address: string;
  addressHelp: string;
  addressRequired: string;
  addressInvalid: string;
  accessStep: string;
  /** The method switch. */
  method: string;
  methodToken: string;
  methodQr: string;
  token: string;
  tokenHelp: string;
  tokenRequired: string;
  /** In QR mode, testing before a code was scanned or delivered. */
  tokenMissing: string;
  qrCode: string;
  qrCaption: string;
  scan: string;
  /** After a scan filled in a token. */
  scanned: string;
  /** The scan found nothing usable. */
  scanEmpty: string;
  testStep: string;
  test: string;
  testing: string;
  success: string;
  failed: string;
  finish: string;
  cancel: string;
}
```

## Web example

```ts
import { createDeviceSetup, type DeviceSetupResult, type DeviceSetupValues } from '@mosaic-home/design-system/web';

async function testServer({ address, token }: DeviceSetupValues): Promise<DeviceSetupResult> {
  try {
    const response = await fetch(address, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
    if (response.status === 401 || response.status === 403) {
      return { ok: false, field: 'token', message: 'The server refused that token' };
    }
    return response.ok ? { ok: true } : { ok: false, message: `The server answered ${response.status}` };
  } catch {
    return { ok: false, field: 'address', message: 'No server answered at that address' };
  }
}

const setup = createDeviceSetup({
  placeholder: 'http://homeassistant.local:8123',
  intro: 'This screen talks to your home server directly.',
  onTest: testServer,
  onFinish: ({ address }) => setup.el.replaceWith(`Connected to ${address}`),
  onCancel: () => setup.el.remove(),
});

document.body.append(setup.el);
```

## React API

`DeviceSetup` (types in `dist/react/home-security.d.ts`): Same DOM and classes as `createDeviceSetup`. `address` and `token` are starting values; a later change of eitherprop fills it in (a delivered pairing). The component sends nothing itself.

## React example

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { DeviceSetup } from '@mosaic-home/design-system/react';
import type { DeviceSetupResult, DeviceSetupValues } from '@mosaic-home/design-system/web';

async function testServer({ address, token }: DeviceSetupValues): Promise<DeviceSetupResult> {
  try {
    const response = await fetch(address, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
    if (response.status === 401 || response.status === 403) {
      return { ok: false, field: 'token', message: 'The server refused that token' };
    }
    return response.ok ? { ok: true } : { ok: false, message: `The server answered ${response.status}` };
  } catch {
    return { ok: false, field: 'address', message: 'No server answered at that address' };
  }
}

export function DeviceSetupExample() {
  const [server, setServer] = useState<string | null>(null);
  if (server) return <p>Connected to {server}</p>;
  return (
    <DeviceSetup
      placeholder="http://homeassistant.local:8123"
      intro="This screen talks to your home server directly."
      onTest={testServer}
      onFinish={({ address }) => setServer(address)}
    />
  );
}
```
